mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5% for three months, contradicting the predicted negative direction.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and inflation expectations, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly decline in real GDP growth below 1% for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth < 1% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where GDPC1 growth is below 1% for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in the industrial production index of more than 0.5% signals a sharp decline in manufacturing activity, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO falls by more than 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% signals a broad-based collapse in household demand, which depresses earnings and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change < -1% AND HOUST monthly change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where both RSAFS and HOUST decline by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid reduction in the federal funds rate by at least 0.75 percentage points within a single month signals an emergency monetary easing, which boosts risk appetite and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: financial crisis or emergency easing episode
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS is cut by at least 0.75% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the unemployment rate and payrolls above their prior-month levels is impossible; however, a large positive revision to payrolls (PAYEMS) while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises signals underemployment expansion, which temporarily boosts corporate revenues but does not improve profit margins, resulting in muted S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS revised up > 0.2% AND UNRATE monthly change > 0.2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of episodes where PAYEMS is revised up > 0.2% while UNRATE rises > 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized CPI inflation above 5% for four consecutive months signals a high-inflation regime, which erodes real corporate earnings and increases discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL year-over-year change > 5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where CPIAUCSL exceeds 5% year-over-year for four consecutive months.
